items.content_html:
Description

Adds a note to the Fetch Metadata Request Headers page clarifying that Fetch Metadata headers are only sent for potentially trustworthy URLs. This helps explain why headers such as Sec-Fetch-Dest, Sec-Fetch-Mode, and Sec-Fetch-Site may be absent on non-secure http:// origins during development and testing.

Motivation

We have a project where we use the Sec-Fetch-Dest header to test whether the content is in an iframe or not and return different content based on that. Worked locally but our non-production deployments did not use https. So this caught us by surprise and I thought a note like this might be helpful to other devs.

Additional details

https://www.w3.org/TR/secure-contexts/#potentially-trustworthy-url

Related issues and pull requests

No related issues or PRs.
items.title: Add note about Fetch Metadata headers on non-secure origins

items.content_html:
Description

I want to make the limitations of checkVisibility more obvious. For example when an element is occluded the checkVisibility method may still return true.

Motivation

The current version claims this:

checks whether the element is visible

while the spec uses more careful wording:

whether an element is potentially "visible"

I think this is slightly misleading as there are many cases in which an element is not visible to the user but this method still returns true. Even with all the optional checks enabled.

Additional details

Specification

items.content_html:
Description

Updates the display property documentation to include the new masonry layout display values grid-lanes and inline-grid-lanes. Also updates the Masonry layout guide to use the current browser compatibility keys and adds cross-references between the two pages.

Motivation

The Masonry layout guide already documents the new masonry implementation based on display: grid-lanes and display: inline-grid-lanes, but the display property page was missing syntax and descriptive documentation for these values. In addition, the Masonry layout guide was still using outdated browser compatibility keys. These changes keep the documentation aligned with the current specification and browser implementation.

Additional details

Changes included in this PR:

  • Updated the Masonry layout guide browser compatibility references:

    • css.properties.grid-template-columns.masonry → css.properties.display.grid-lanes
    • css.properties.grid-template-rows.masonry → css.properties.display.inline-grid-lanes

  • Added display: grid-lanes; and display: inline-grid-lanes; to the display property syntax section.

  • Added descriptions for both grid-lanes and inline-grid-lanes.

  • Added grid-lanes and inline-grid-lanes to the display comparison example selector.

  • Added cross-links between the display property page and the Masonry layout guide.

Related issues and pull requests

Fixes #44421
items.title: [CSS] Add grid-lanes documentation to display property

This adds that context in one reference location instead of repeating it across individual element pages.

Summary

  • clarify how badge, icon, and image serve different purposes in showNotification() options
  • note that notification UI rendering varies by platform and that visual options should not carry essential information by themselves

items.content_html:
Description

  • Fixes description of composite transform to use left-to-right order instead of right-to-left.

Motivation

The composite transform example in animation-composition originally described the process from left-to-right, with each transform establishing a new coordinate space. This was changed to the right-to-left order in #38561 because at the time, the docs for transform were worded such that it seemed that right-to-left was "the order" in practice.

With #43496, the transform docs are much clearer on the different orders and respective behaviours with coordinate space, and uses the left-to-right order as the primary one for explanation. Therefore, we can return the animation-composition example to how it was before.

Description

Makes the experimental status of a feature of color-mix explicit.

Motivation

The color list feature is described in pretty much the whole page just like it would be if it was already supported widely. I think adding information directly on this page to highlight what part of color-mix is still experimental is relevant. This lack of clarity caused a minor bug on the xwiki-platform project and I hope this change can help other devs :)

Ideally the formal syntax would be updated too. I'm not well-versed in it so I won't propose it myself.

Thank you for your consideration!

Additional details

Bug raised for xwiki-platform: https://jira.xwiki.org/browse/XWIKI-24472
